worldcombat.skill.submission.summary: Lunge in, grab a target and slam it down: a hit deals contact damage, and if the target can be moved it is knocked down and sharply slowed while the user takes a share of the damage as recoil. A target that cannot be moved instead takes a standing grapple strike - same damage, but it is not knocked down. A bulkier target takes a lighter slam and a shorter pin; a whiff has neither damage nor recoil.
worldcombat.skill.submission.description: The user lunges in, grabs the target and slams it down for about %1$s contact damage; it lunges up to %2$s blocks at %3$s blocks per tick with a %4$s block grab radius.

After the grab a %1$s s window passes: the target is held and cannot move, and the user is rooted too; it is then slammed - a target that can be moved is pinned for %2$s s and hurled %3$s blocks, while one that cannot be moved just takes the slam damage and is not knocked down. A bulkier target takes less slam damage and is pinned for less time.
On a hit the user takes %1$s times the actual damage as recoil.
worldcombat.skill.submission.pin.on: Pinning form: a lighter slam and less recoil, but the target is held down much longer - for control and team play.
worldcombat.skill.submission.pin.off: Throwing form: a heavier slam, a wider throw and more recoil, but the target is up again quickly.
worldcombat.skill.submission.timing: Range %1$s blocks; wind-up %2$s s, recovery %3$s s, cooldown %4$s s, costing %5$s PP.
worldcombat.skill.submission.growth.0: From level %1$s the slam power rises to %2$s.
worldcombat.skill.submission.growth.1: From level %1$s the slam power rises to %2$s and the pin lasts %3$s s.
worldcombat.skill.submission.use.0: Grab and pin a target in your face to open a window for allies
worldcombat.skill.submission.use.1: Grab an adjacent foe and hold it in place for a while
worldcombat.skill.submission.use.2: Nail a target down with the pin, taking the recoil yourself

worldcombat.skill.submission.description: While knocked down the target cannot get up and moves much slower; as long as it is still held and can be moved, it is pinned even if the slam deals no damage. Losing the grip or being pulled too far apart ends the grapple - no remote throw.
